candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation: reduce orders when pipeline is high relative to recent demand, especially at upstream nodes, to avoid over-ordering and excess inventory/backlog. Node0 reduces if pipeline exceeds 3x recent demand; node1 reduces if pipeline exceeds 2x recent demand; node2 reduces if pipeline exceeds 2x recent demand. Small negative deltas.

Backlog-driven increase: if backlog is high, increase orders to replenish, but cap increase to avoid overshoot. Node0 increases by 1 if backlog>0; node1 increases by 2 if backlog>10; node2 increases by 2 if backlog>20. Also, if inventory is zero and backlog positive, increase by 1 for all nodes.

Demand-growth response: if recent demand exceeds baseline (growth>1), increase orders proportionally to growth, but only if pipeline is not excessive. Node0 increases by 2 if growth>1.1; node1 increases by 2 if growth>1.1 and pipeline<2*recent; node2 increases by 2 if growth>1.1 and pipeline<2*recent. Otherwise no change.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

candidates.explanation: Moderate pipeline-aware increase at all nodes when recent demand exceeds baseline, with extra boost at node0 to protect downstream service. Caps prevent overordering.
Aggressive increase at node0 when recent demand exceeds baseline, with smaller increases at upstream nodes to avoid overreaction. Backlog triggers additional orders.
Conservative increase only when demand is significantly above baseline and inventory is low, with pipeline-aware cap to avoid overordering.

candidates.explanation: Coordinated pipeline-aware relaxation: node0 and node1 reduce orders when their backlog is high and pipeline is large, while node2 increases orders to replenish upstream and avoid starving downstream. This reduces total inventory+backlog by preventing over-ordering at upstream nodes that already have sufficient pipeline, and ensures node2 has enough supply to meet future demand.

Demand-responsive correction: increase orders at all nodes when recent demand exceeds baseline (growth>1.05) to build inventory ahead of potential emergency, but cap increases when backlog is already high to avoid exacerbating upstream backlog. Node2 gets a larger increase because it is the supply source.

Backlog-clearing and pipeline-balancing: nodes with high backlog relative to pipeline increase orders to clear backlog faster, while nodes with low backlog and high pipeline reduce orders to avoid excess inventory. Node2 always orders at least its incoming demand to prevent upstream starvation.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.

Backlog-driven: when backlog is high, increase orders to clear it; when backlog is low and inventory is high, decrease orders to reduce holding cost.

Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.

Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.

Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

candidates.explanation: Coordinated pipeline-aware relaxation: node0 and node1 reduce orders when backlog is high and pipeline is sufficient, while node2 maintains orders to replenish upstream. This avoids increasing downstream backlog by not starving node0 and node1, and reduces total cost by preventing excessive inventory and backlog accumulation.

Demand-responsive adjustment: when recent demand is below baseline (growth<1), reduce orders to avoid overstock; when growth>1, increase orders to meet potential surge. Node0 and node1 adjust based on their backlog, while node2 uses inventory to decide. This balances cost and service by aligning orders with observed demand trends.

Backlog-clearing and pipeline smoothing: nodes with high backlog and low inventory increase orders to clear backlog, but only if pipeline is not already excessive. Node2 reduces orders if inventory is high to prevent upstream backlog. This rule set aims to reduce downstream backlog while avoiding starvation.

rules.when: agent==0 and backlog>15 and inventory<5 and pipeline<80
